title: Time reports keep hours clocked on internal work orders
custom_preconds:
Preconditions

  • Sign in as an Admin at the test location.
  • Make sure the Internal Work Orders setting is on in Settings > Work Orders.
  • Have technician A for this test, with no time clocked to a department.
  • Have a new customer for this test, customer A, flagged as an Internal customer.
  • Have a new internal work order for this test, work order 1, for internal customer A, closed today, on which technician A clocked 2.0 hours.
custom_steps:
1. Open Reports > Shop Efficiency.
  2. Open Reports > Technician Utilization.
  3. Open Timesheets for technician A today.
custom_expected:
Expected Result

Step 1:

  • Technician A's 2.0 hours count as worked hours.
  • Technician A's "Internal Hours" shows no hours: the 2.0 hours on work order 1 are not counted there (that column counts time clocked to a department).

Step 2:

  • Technician A's 2.0 hours count as worked hours.

Step 3:

  • The 2.0 hours on work order 1 are listed.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

From: PRD "Internal Work Orders (PRD)", Confluence 942243841, version 1.0 final (9 Nov 2026, Milos Vasic), read 12 Nov 2026 · Epic SV-11665, story SV-11766 (Story 9, Reports, dashboard and exports)

  • S9-R8: “Shop Efficiency, Technician Utilization and Timesheets keep clocked hours on internal and no-charge work orders and on no-charge lines as worked hours; Shop Efficiency leaves a no-charge line's estimated hours out of invoiced hours; the existing "Internal Hours" column (time clocked to a department, not to a work order) is unchanged and unrelated.”
